recent_posts.title: How AI coding agents are outpacing traditional vulnerability management
recent_posts.summary: AI coding agents like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot are dramatically accelerating development cycles, with 64% of organizations already using AI to generate most of their code. However, this speed introduces new security risks: higher bug rates, identity sprawl, untracked assets, and an expanded attack surface that traditional vulnerability management tools weren't designed to handle. Traditional VM tools rely on baselines and CVE signatures, but AI-generated code creates non-deterministic, context-dependent risks that appear between scans. The post argues that Continuous Exposure Management is the appropriate security paradigm for the AI era, capable of mapping attack paths, prioritizing real exposures beyond CVEs, and catching flaws pre-deployment.

recent_posts.title: How to Develop a Risk Management Framework
recent_posts.summary: A guide to building a cybersecurity risk management framework, covering five key steps: identifying risks, analyzing and prioritizing them, strategic mitigation (accept, avoid, transfer, reduce), continuous monitoring, and leveraging technology. The post also highlights the strategic value of formal frameworks for business alignment, regulatory compliance (ISO 27001, NIST), and operational efficiency. Sponsored content promotes LogicManager ERM software as a solution for automating the risk lifecycle.

recent_posts.title: How supply chain attacks exploit trusted vendor relationships across ecosystems
recent_posts.summary: Supply chain attacks are increasingly targeting trust relationships between organizations rather than individual companies. A single compromised vendor, SaaS provider, or API integration can cascade access across multiple downstream organizations. Credentials like API keys and service tokens are central to these attacks, often operating undetected because activity appears legitimate. Early warning signals frequently emerge outside internal environments — in dark web forums, exposed repositories, and leaked credentials — making external visibility and cyber signal intelligence critical for proactive defense.

recent_posts.title: Mallory Launches AI-Native Threat Intelligence Platform, Turning Global Threat Data Into Prioritized Action
recent_posts.summary: Mallory, an AI-native threat intelligence platform, has launched out of stealth with seed funding led by Decibel Partners. Built by veteran security practitioners and led by a former Google and Mandiant executive, the platform monitors thousands of threat sources, contextualizes them against an organization's actual attack surface, and delivers prioritized, evidence-based action items rather than raw alerts. It integrates with existing security tools and supports Claude Code, MCP, and API access. A 30-day free trial is available immediately.

recent_posts.title: SpyCloud 2026 report finds surge in API key and machine identity theft
recent_posts.summary: SpyCloud's 2026 Identity Exposure Report documents a sharp rise in non-human identity (NHI) theft, with 18.1 million exposed API keys and tokens and 6.2 million credentials tied to AI tools recaptured in 2025. The report highlights that attackers are increasingly targeting session tokens, authentication cookies, and machine credentials alongside traditional username/password pairs. Key findings include 8.6 billion stolen cookies and session artifacts, 642.4 million credentials from 13.2 million infostealer infections, phishing surging 400% YoY with 28.6 million phished records, and 80% of exposed corporate credentials containing plaintext passwords. The report warns that NHIs often lack MFA enforcement and rotate infrequently, making them high-value targets with broad access to cloud and enterprise systems.

recent_posts.title: Top security operations consulting firms for government contractors
recent_posts.summary: A curated list of five security operations consulting firms suited for government contractors navigating CMMC, NIST 800-171, and DFARS requirements. The firms covered are SEC.co (broad SECops and compliance), Mandiant (threat intelligence and incident response), MAD Security (CMMC-certified with 24/7 SOC), GuidePoint Security (SOC design and MDR optimization), and Endurance IT (smaller contractors needing DoD compliance guidance). Each entry highlights the specific strengths and use cases that make the firm relevant to federal contractors.

recent_posts.title: Why performance testing matters before launch and who can help
recent_posts.summary: Performance testing is often overlooked until a product launch fails under real user load. Unlike basic functional checks, performance testing simulates massive traffic spikes to expose bottlenecks before customers encounter them. Outsourcing this to specialized firms like TestingXperts, ScienceSoft, Testfort, and QA Mentor can reveal issues developers miss because they know their own software too well. With research showing users abandon pages that take over three seconds to load, investing in pre-launch performance testing is framed as essential to protecting revenue.

recent_posts.title: One Identity Appoints Michael Henricks as Chief Financial and Operating Officer
recent_posts.summary: One Identity has appointed Michael Henricks as Chief Financial and Operating Officer. Henricks brings over 30 years of experience across technology, business services, and financial services, most recently serving as CEO and CFO at Momentive Software. His role will encompass traditional CFO responsibilities alongside strategic planning and operational-financial integration as One Identity continues to scale, supporting more than 11,000 organizations and managing over 500 million identities worldwide.

recent_posts.title: The Next Wave: A Comparative Review of Leading GenAI Testing Tools
recent_posts.summary: GenAI testing tools are reshaping QA by replacing static, script-based automation with intelligent, adaptive systems. Key capabilities include natural language test case generation, self-healing test execution, predictive analytics for risk identification, visual UI validation, and synthetic test data generation. The article highlights TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest KaneAI) as a featured platform, covering its natural language-driven test creation, cross-platform support, and CI/CD integration. Evaluation criteria for choosing GenAI testing platforms include intelligence depth, scalability, maintenance reduction, integration readiness, and actionability of insights. Future directions point toward fully autonomous testing agents, behavioral analysis, and predictive risk modeling across the entire software lifecycle.

recent_posts.title: Protecting Your Brand: Why You Need Modern Visual Regression Testing Tools
recent_posts.summary: Visual regression testing has become essential for teams shipping UI-heavy applications across diverse browsers and devices. Manual screenshot comparison no longer scales with modern development velocity. Modern visual regression tools use cloud automation, AI-powered smart diffing, and CI/CD integration to catch unintended UI changes before they reach production. Key capabilities include parallel cross-browser execution, noise-reducing comparison engines, versioned baselines, and combined visual/accessibility validation. The article promotes TestMu AI as an all-in-one platform offering these features, arguing that automated visual testing reduces production defects, speeds release cycles, and protects brand trust.

top_posts.summary: Brave Browser turns your device into a Proxy Via “Snowflake’s Snowflake” feature. Activating this option allows users to volunteer their device as a proxy, enabling other users to access Tor in repressive regions.

top_posts.title: How to check suspicious links fast?
top_posts.summary: Cyber attackers are becoming more sophisticated, so it's crucial to use up-to-date tools like ANY.RUN’s Safebrowsing to check suspicious links. This tool allows you to enter a URL into a secure environment for fast analysis. You can navigate the site safely, receive alerts about malicious activities, and generate detailed reports on potential threats. Organizations can empower employees to use these tools to prevent phishing attacks without needing security team intervention.

top_posts.title: Google Chrome uBlock Origin Users Need To Switch Ad Blocker
top_posts.summary: Google Chrome users will need to switch from uBlock Origin to other ad blockers as the extension will no longer be supported due to Chrome Manifest V3 policies. The developers suggest using uBO Lite, a Manifest V3-compliant version with fewer features. Users must manually install uBO Lite as it won't automatically upgrade from uBlock Origin. Firefox and other browsers still support uBlock Origin.

top_posts.title: Mozilla Released Firefox 130 With Handy AI Chatbot Feature And Security Fixes
top_posts.summary: Firefox 130 brings significant updates, including the integration of an AI chatbot under the new 'Firefox Labs' feature. Users can customize their chat preferences with a variety of chatbots like ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The update also introduces auto picture-in-picture, improved language translation, and input method editor (IME) support for complex symbols. Importantly, the release addresses several security vulnerabilities, making it vital for users to update.

top_posts.title: Researchers Demonstrate Windows Downgrade Attacks At Black Hat 2024
top_posts.summary: Researchers from SafeBreach have unveiled 'Downgrade attacks' at Black Hat 2024, exploiting two zero-day vulnerabilities to revert updated Windows systems to their vulnerable states. These attacks, involving privilege escalation flaws (CVE-2024-38202 and CVE-2024-21302), allow attackers to bypass security features and reintroduce previously patched vulnerabilities. The researchers demonstrated that these attacks could compromise OS components without physical access. Microsoft is currently working on mitigation strategies.
